greeting.text: Welcome to the Guild, {player}. I am {npc}, one of the advisers. Everything you do below goes into a record, and I would like yours to be a long one.
New face, new page. I am {npc}. Tell me your name and what you can do, {player}, and I will tell you which floors are sensible.
Back safely, {player}. Good. That is the only result the Guild truly cares about.
Sit down for a moment, {player}. Your record will not write itself.
The board is quiet today. In my experience that means somebody is about to do something foolish. Not you, I hope.
Rested, supplied, rope, light? Then go. And come back.

hint.text: Every adventurer and every monster has a Level in the Guild's books. A Level is a measure of how much a body has been through, and the Dungeon seems to notice it.
When a monster is nearly beaten, the Dungeon looks at the party. A party that is strong enough meets a monster that is stronger than it was a moment ago. That is not unfair, it is the Dungeon.
Do not fight a monster above your Level with a party below it. Fear is not a figure of speech down there: some of them can make you slow, and weak. Anti-magic does not care about that kind of noise.
The Guild pays for stones and for information. A fight you can describe to me is worth more than a fight you only survived.

A Minotaur has been seen on the upper floors, where nothing of its kind should be. The Guild rates it Level 2. It picks the weakest of a party and does not let go; put a wall at your back and let it run into it.

The Minotaur is down, and the Guild has put it in your record. Now the reports from the lower floors: the stone Goliath of the pit first, and behind it a Goliath that is the wrong colour. Black as slate, and plain swords glance off it. Bring something heavy, or a spell.

Beyond the giant's floor there is a city half under water, and something with two heads lives in it. One head breathes a flame that eats steel, the other a mist that eats magic. Take the red one first.
The White Palace is the last page the Guild has for now: a skeleton as tall as a house, with a black sword and ribs that turn to meet every blow. Do not strike it from one side only.
That is every great monster the Guild has a page for. I will have to write new pages. The Dungeon never runs out of material; do not let that make you careless.

quest_offer.text: There is an open request at the counter, {player}: the Minotaur on the upper floors, a Level 2 where there should be none. Bring it down and I will mark the request done. Take friends; it prefers the weakest of them.
The Guild would like the Minotaur off the upper floors before it kills somebody's first expedition. Will you take the request, {player}? Bring it down and tell me how it went.

quest_done.text: You brought the Minotaur down. I have written it in your record, with today's date and a very long underline. Thank you, {player}.
The Minotaur is finished, and nobody had to carry anybody home. That is the best report I have had all month, {player}.

farewell.text: Come back with all your fingers.
Go on. And write down what you see.
The Guild thanks you for your custom.
